messages.content: Why do we keep matches and lighters out of small children's reach?
To prevent fires and burns. Because young children are curious and do not yet understand the danger, so they might strike a match and hurt themselves.
Why do we need to shake a bottle of mango juice that has settled?
The thick parts sink to the bottom. Because they are heavier than the watery part, so they slowly drift down when the bottle stands still.
I have a test tomorrow and a game tonight. How can I decide what to do?
Think about which matters more and whether both are possible. Because you may be able to study first and play later, and weighing the two helps you avoid regrets.
Why is it good to thank someone who has helped us?
The helper feels valued. Because thanking shows that we noticed the help, the helper is more likely to help again.
Why does hot air rise above a flame?
Warm air is lighter than the cool air around it. Because heated air spreads out, the cooler air sinks in and pushes it upwards.
Why does a cool breeze blow from the sea towards the land in the afternoon?
The land has become warmer than the sea. Because warm air above the land rises and cooler air from the sea moves in to fill the space, we feel a breeze from the water.
Why do people have two eyes and not just one?
Eyes working as a pair help us judge how far away things are. Because each eye sees from a slightly different spot, the brain compares the pictures and works out depth.
Why is it fair for every person in the house to help with the chores?

Sharing the chores spreads the work across everyone who lives in the house. Because the work would pile up on one person if the rest did nothing, sharing the tasks keeps any one person from being worn out.
Why does a pencil leave a mark on paper?
A little of the pencil's lead wears off onto the paper. Because the soft graphite breaks into tiny flakes as it rubs over the rough surface, the flakes stay caught in the paper and form the line.
Why must a fair test change only the thing we are studying?

Keeping everything else the same lets us link the result to the thing we study. Because if other things change as well, we cannot tell which of them caused the result, the result would not teach us anything certain.
Why should a child tell a trusted adult where they are going when they go out to play?
Telling an adult means help can be found quickly. Because the adult then knows where to look if plans change or something goes wrong, a problem does not stay hidden for long.
Why can music change our mood so quickly?
Music acts on both the body and memory. Because the rhythm and tune make us move, breathe and feel in time with them, and a song can also bring back happy or sad memories, the feeling shifts.
Why does the sun seem to rise in the east?

The sun only seems to move; the Earth turning towards the east brings the sun into view from the east. Because our own spot is carried around with the spinning Earth, we are turned toward the sun in the morning from that side, and it appears to climb into the sky.
Why does a kind word from a friend lift our mood?
A kind word makes us feel valued and eases worry. Because people need to feel that others accept them, a warm remark brings the pleasant feeling of belonging.
If it is a holiday, the market is crowded. The market is crowded. Is it a holiday?
We cannot be sure. Because crowds can gather for a festival, a sale or a weekend as well, a crowded market does not by itself prove a holiday.
How does a spider catch insects without chasing them?

Many spiders let a web do the catching. Because the threads are thin, sticky and hard for a flying insect to see, a bug that blunders into them gets stuck, and the spider feels the shaking and walks over.
Why do sand dunes slowly move across the desert?
The wind carries sand grains up the gentle side. Because the grains tumble down the steep far side and settle there, the whole dune creeps forward.
One box has 9 pencils. How many pencils are in 9 boxes?
81. Because 9 x 9 = 81, so 9 boxes hold 81 pencils.
I need 4 groups of 2 stickers. How many stickers is that?
8. Because 4 x 2 = 8, so 4 groups of 2 make 8 stickers.
A train stops at 9 stations before noon and 8 stations after noon. How many stops is that?
17. Because 9 + 8 = 17, so that is 17 stops.
